WEEK 1 PREDICTIONS — RECALIBRATED

The schedule is out, team names have changed and the defense rules have been rebuilt because Sleeper cannot apply negative scoring only after 10 points or 300 yards. Under the new setup, defenses are no longer handed free points for simply existing. Points allowed are penalized continuously, yardage penalties begin at 300, and impact plays—sacks, turnovers, tackles for loss, passes defended, three-and-outs and fourth-down stops—matter more. That pulls most defenses into a tighter range and makes one touchdown or one complete defensive collapse capable of swinging a matchup.

These are SRS-style fantasy projections using the current starting lineups, the updated CPBFFL scoring, Week 1 player expectations and matchup context. Week 1 is still calibration mode, so everyone may begin preparing their excuses now.

TEAM 3 VS. YOKIEL — Pick: Tony Yokiel, 120.3–118.0. Tony finally dropped The Bye Week name, apparently hoping a rebrand would make everyone forget that he drafted Houston’s defense 100th overall. It did not. Puka projects as the biggest player in this matchup at roughly 20.5, with Hurts around 18.8. Steve answers with JSN near 19.7, Derrick Henry and Bucky Irving, plus enough tight ends to survive a position apocalypse that is not happening. New defensive scoring slightly favors New England over Houston, but not enough to save Steve. Tony wins a close one and immediately acts like the defense reach was genius.

VRABELS LLC VS. SPEAKSOONSTAYLUCKY — Pick: Matt Rennert, 125.9–123.2. This may be the best Week 1 matchup that did not receive the Game of the Week label. Mike brings Josh Allen, Christian McCaffrey, Kyren Williams, Tee Higgins and DK Metcalf. Matt counters with Gibbs, Bowers, Garrett Wilson, Brian Thomas Jr. and enough depth to survive an actual injury. McCaffrey and Gibbs both project above 21 points, so this could become a heavyweight fight quickly. Denver’s defense takes a little more punishment under the revised rules than Seattle, giving Matt another small edge. The village idiot escapes by fewer than three.

DOUBLE DRAKE VS. MCGIBBLETS MUNCHKIN GUILD — Pick: John DeBrouse, 118.7–118.4. Yes, that says John. No, the model has not been hacked. The old projection leaned Jake; the updated scoring turns this into a virtual coin flip and gives John the edge by approximately three-tenths of a point. Jake still leads the historical series 6-5 and will absolutely claim fraud if he loses by a defensive pass breakup. This is the Upset Special.

INJURYAPOLIS COLTS VS. YOURDADD — Pick: Reid Masters, 119.4–113.8. Bijan is the highest projection in this matchup at roughly 21.7, and Reid has the more complete lineup from top to bottom. Sam still has Cook, Chase Brown, Caleb Williams and enough young talent to make this uncomfortable—but he currently has no defense selected. Under the revised scoring, an average Week 1 defense projects around four to seven points, so filling that spot could turn this into a near toss-up. Until then, Reid owns the roster edge, the model edge and a 3-0 historical record against Sam. The former final boss is once again fighting with one hand tied behind his back, except this time he tied it himself.

GAME OF THE WEEK — COMMISSIONER STILL SUCKS VS. SUNDAY CRUISERS — Pick: Erik Mannarino, 116.7–114.4. The defending champion faces the #2 post-draft team in a Central Division heavyweight fight. Brian gets a major defensive-scoring advantage: Jacksonville projects near 7.7 while the Rams sit around 4.2. Amon-Ra also carries the highest individual expectation in the matchup at roughly 19.8. Erik still has the safer overall build with Burrow, Jonathan Taylor, Saquon and Trey McBride. Brian’s rookies give him the bigger explosion range, but Erik has fewer ways for the entire lineup to shit itself at once. Brian leads the career series 10-7; Erik gets Week 1 by a field goal or less.

LITTLE DOWNIES VS. DEUTSCH4988 — Pick: Paul Deutsch, 125.7–119.3. The corrected 2025 history now shows Paul winning last season, because apparently ruining my week is not a hobby for him—it is a documented tradition. Chase and Nico Collins give Paul two elite projection anchors, while Jaxson Dart only needs to avoid setting the quarterback position on fire. Shawn has Jayden Daniels, Justin Jefferson, Olave and two rookie running backs with real ceiling, but Pittsburgh’s defense carries a modest Week 1 edge over Minnesota under the new rules. The revised model cuts the old projected margin from roughly ten to about six. That is close enough for hope, which is exactly how Paul prefers to make the eventual disappointment hurt.

2026 FINAL STANDINGS & CHAMPION PREDICTION

This forecast blends roster strength, current starter projections, depth, the 14-week schedule, revised defensive scoring and a 20,000-season SRS-style simulation. Matt and Reid draw the friendliest schedules among the contenders. Steve, Tony, Brian and Sam face the roughest paths. This is not a promise; it is simply the computer volunteering to become the next league member everyone can tell to go fuck itself.

1. VRABELS LLC — Matt Rennert — PROJECTED CHAMPION. The deepest roster, the strongest Week 1 projection and approximately a 36% title chance. If Gibbs and Bowers stay healthy, Matt may become completely unbearable.

2. DEUTSCH4988 — Paul Deutsch. Chase, Nico, Breece and Flowers create a massive weekly ceiling. Approximately an 18% title chance, plus a 100% chance Paul gets sniped immediately before at least one waiver claim.

3. INJURYAPOLIS COLTS — Reid Masters. Bijan gives Reid the safest foundation in the league, and the schedule helps. Roughly a 10% title chance. Seniority continues to mean absolutely nothing to him.

4. SPEAKSOONSTAYLUCKY — Michael Clark. Allen and McCaffrey can drag this roster into the championship conversation by themselves. Roughly an 8% title chance. The entire forecast depends on CMC’s body remaining attached.

5. SUNDAY CRUISERS — Erik Mannarino. Taylor, Saquon, Burrow and McBride may be the league’s best starting core. Roughly a 7% title chance, with enough depth to outperform this ranking.

6. MCGIBBLETS MUNCHKIN GUILD — Jake Stacy. Lamar, Achane and A.J. Brown make Jake dangerous every week. Roughly a 6% title chance. The roster is a contender; the owner remains the largest security vulnerability.

7. LITTLE DOWNIES — Shawn Smutak. Strong starters, dangerous rookies and almost no margin for injury. Roughly a 5% title chance. The model predicts another year of researching everything except how to win the final game.

8. COMMISSIONER STILL SUCKS — Brian Corrigan. The defending champion has enormous rookie upside but one of the tougher schedules. Roughly a 3% title chance. If Jeanty, Judkins and Nabers all hit, this ranking will look idiotic by October.

9. YOKIEL — Tony Yokiel. Puka and Hurts keep Tony alive, but the depth and schedule are less forgiving. Roughly a 3% title chance. Changing the team name does not erase the defense pick.

10. DOUBLE DRAKE — John DeBrouse. CeeDee, London and Maye give John a real weekly path. Roughly a 2% title chance. The model likes him more than the league does, which is the lowest possible bar.

11. TEAM 3 — Steve Cegelka. Good starters, useful depth and the hardest projected schedule in the league. Roughly a 2% title chance. If the league unexpectedly changes to three starting tight ends, move Steve directly to number one.

12. YOURDADD — Sam Young. Cook and Chase Brown are good; the roster still needs help and the schedule offers none. Less than a 1% title chance. Sam may remain the career wins leader, but the model sees the castle continuing to crumble.

CHAMPION: MATT RENNERT — VRABELS LLC. Congratulations to Matt on winning a championship that currently exists only inside a simulation. I am sure he will celebrate it with the restraint and humility for which he is famous.
